overview: White plays the waiting move 1.a3, a prophylactic idea that prepares b4 or a Sicilian/English reversed with an extra tempo for queenside expansion. After 1...e5 or 1...d5 White usually plays e3, c4 or g3 and Bg2. It is slow, flexible and transposes to many structures.

white_ideas.idea: Play b4 and Bb2 or a flexible English set-up with an extra tempo on the queenside.
Fianchetto the king's bishop and keep the centre options open.

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...e5 or ...d5 and develop freely.
Gain time since a3 does little for development.

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Sicilian or English structures with a3 played early.

soundness.notes: Not refuted but loses a tempo.

structure.notes: Flank first move leaving the centre undecided.

level.notes: Easy to play but not a good first repertoire.

soundness.reason: A tempo down but not refuted.

level.reason: Simple but not a good base repertoire.
